title: Automating 4D Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy for High-Throughput Data Acquisition
content: 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) is a powerful and versatile analysis tool that collects full 2D diffraction patterns at each STEM probe position in 2D real space. This generates four-dimensional datasets from which information about a broad range of sample properties can be extracted, such as structure [1], composition [2], defects [3] and electric and magnetic fields [4]. However, the throughput of 4D-STEM experiments is often limited by the slow readout speeds of 4D detectors – typically 100-1000x slower than standard STEM detectors [5] – which results in individual 4D scans often taking tens of minutes to acquire [5]. Even when faster detectors are used, the large file size of 4D datasets (100s GBs – TBs) presents additional challenges to throughput. Storing more than a dozen or so raw 4D datasets at any one time is difficult on common hard drives, meaning data must be offloaded or hard drives changed frequently. Additionally, processing such large datasets can only be performed efficiently by high-end edge computers or supercomputers, slowing the speed at which useful information can be obtained from 4D-STEM experiments.
